newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan seen buying, corn, soybeans and wheat.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan seen buying, corn, soybeans and wheat.

text.p: Taiwanese importers are expected in the market this week for a total of 74,000 tonnes of U.S. corn and 118,000 tonnes of U.S. soybeans, local traders said on Monday.
The Taiwan Flour Mills Association was also seen placing tenders for three wheat shipments within two weeks, they said.

Members Feed Industry Group could retender for a 54,000-tonne shipment of U.S. No.2 corn on which it passed on July 26. The shipment was scheduled for delivery from October 1-15 from the U.S. Gulf or October 16-30 from the Pacific Northwest.
State-owned Taiwan Sugar Corp said it would hold a tender for a combined shipment of 20,000 tonnes of U.S. No.2 corn and 10,000 tonnes of U.S. No.2 soybeans by September 5.
Taiwan Sugar's shipment would be slated for delivery from September 20 to October 5 from the U.S. Gulf or October 5-20 from the Pacific Northwest, traders said.
Taiwan's Breakfast Soybean Procurement Association Taichung division is likely to place a tender for two 54,000-tonne U.S. soybean shipments this week.

The Breakfast Association's Kaohsiung division bought two 54,000-tonne consignments of U.S. soybeans at an August 23 tender. The prices of these purchases would be used by the Taichung division as a benchmark, traders said.
"The Taichung division is likely to follow the Breakfast Association Kaohsiung division's tender on Friday and benchmark its prices," a trader said.
Traders said they expected the Taiwan Flour Mills Association to purchase two 34,000-tonne shipments and one shipment of around 26,000 tonnes of wheat in the next two weeks.
"A total of three shipments will be tendered soon, but one shipment's size still needs to be decided," Flour Association official Lu Wei-chih said.

"Our buyers are still registering their needs for the next round of tenders for the latter half of the year's supplies. "Most buyers consider that CBOT (Chicago Board of Trade) wheat prices look good right now," he said.

Taiwan's provincial Food Bureau will tender on August 28 for a 15,470-tonne combined shipment of U.S. No.1 wheat, traders said. The shipment is slated for delivery from the Pacific Northwest between October 1 to 20.
The shipment comprises 7,700 tonnes of hard red winter wheat and 7,770 tonnes of soft wheat, traders said.
The local price of wheat flour for Taipei delivery ranged between T$14.55 to T$15.68 a kg, unchanged from a week ago.
The domestic soymeal price for Taipei delivery was quoted at between T$9.5 to T$9.7 a kg, up from T$9.4 a week earlier.
Corn powder was indicated unchanged at T$7.18 a kg for Taipei delivery.

U.S. Pacific Northwest to Taiwan grain freight rates were quoted at about US$10.50 a tonne and from the Gulf of Mexico at about S$20.00 a tonne, both for Panamax-sized September shipments. October shipments were about 50 U.S. cents a tonne higher on each route.
